library(psych)

# Power analysis for the repeated-measures (paired) t-test
### Note: with this small df (9) the textbook will give a higher power than what you see here.
```{r}
PreGroup = sleep$extra[1:10]
PostGroup = sleep$extra[11:20]
diff = PostGroup - PreGroup

# Mean difference, SD of differences, and Cohen's d (explicit calculation)
mean_diff = mean(diff)
sd_diff   = sd(diff)
d         = mean_diff / sd_diff

paste(c("Mean of differences:", mean_diff))
paste(c("SD of differences:", sd_diff))
paste(c("Cohen's d:", d))

# --- Power of the test just demonstrated ---
# For paired: delta = mean of differences, sd = SD of the differences
power.t.test(n = 10,
             delta = mean_diff,
             sd = sd_diff,
             type = "paired")

# --- Sample size needed for a future experiment (80% power) ---
power.t.test(power = 0.80,
             delta = mean_diff,
             sd = sd_diff,
             type = "paired")

```



# Power analysis for the independent-groups t-test (equal n)
### Note: No problem with this higher df (49), but you will still get differences from the hand calculations because the computer is more exact.
```{r}
group1 = iris[iris$Species == "setosa", ]
group2 = iris[iris$Species == "versicolor", ]

# Means, SDs, and pooled SD (explicit calculation)
m1  = mean(group1$Sepal.Length)
m2  = mean(group2$Sepal.Length)
s1  = sd(group1$Sepal.Length)
s2  = sd(group2$Sepal.Length)
n1  = nrow(group1)
n2  = nrow(group2)

sd_pooled = sqrt( ((n1 - 1) * s1^2 + (n2 - 1) * s2^2) / (n1 + n2 - 2) )

paste(c("Pooled SD:", sd_pooled))

# Cohen's d (for reference / comparison with the table)
d = abs(m1 - m2) / sd_pooled

paste(c("Cohen's d:", d))

# --- Power of the test just demonstrated ---
# delta = raw mean difference, sd = pooled SD
power.t.test(n = 50,
             delta = abs(m1 - m2),
             sd = sd_pooled,
             type = "two.sample")

# --- Sample size needed for a future experiment (80% power) ---
power.t.test(power = 0.80,
             delta = abs(m1 - m2),
             sd = sd_pooled,
             type = "two.sample")

```


# Power analysis for the independent-groups t-test (unequal n)
### Note: power.t.test() assumes equal n; the calls below approximate using the smaller group size (n = 20)
```{r}
group1 = iris[iris$Species == "virginica", ]
group2 = iris[iris$Species == "versicolor", ][1:20, ]

# Means, SDs, ns, and pooled SD (explicit calculation)
m1  = mean(group1$Sepal.Width)
m2  = mean(group2$Sepal.Width)
s1  = sd(group1$Sepal.Width)
s2  = sd(group2$Sepal.Width)
n1  = nrow(group1)
n2  = nrow(group2)

sd_pooled = sqrt( ((n1 - 1) * s1^2 + (n2 - 1) * s2^2) / (n1 + n2 - 2) )

paste(c("n1 (virginica):", n1, "  n2 (versicolor subset):", n2))
paste(c("Pooled SD:", sd_pooled))

# Cohen's d (for reference)
d = abs(m1 - m2) / sd_pooled

paste(c("Cohen's d:", d))

# Harmonic mean
n_h <- 2 * n1 * n2 / (n1 + n2)

paste(c("Harmonic Mean:", n_h))

power.t.test(n = n_h,
             delta = abs(m1 - m2),
             sd = sd_pooled,
             type = "two.sample")
# --- Sample size needed for a future experiment (80% power) ---
# This returns the n *per group* under the equal-n assumption
power.t.test(power = 0.80,
             delta = abs(m1 - m2),
             sd = sd_pooled,
             type = "two.sample")

```
